newsitem.title: UK: Pilot panel advises reject Undervalued bid.
newsitem.headline: Pilot panel advises reject Undervalued bid.

text.p: Investment company Pilot Investment Trust Plc said a panel of independent directors was "strongly" recommending that shareholders reject an unsolicited offer from Undervalued Assets Trust.
In a letter to shareholders dated February 4, it said the panel formed in February had been advised to make the recommendation by financial advisor and broker Merrill Lynch.
On February 14, UAT offered seven new shares in its share capital for every nine shares in Pilot, and 33 pence for each Pilot warrant.
Pilot said in a statement that the offer represented only a 5.4 percent increase in the capital value of Pilot shares as at February 11, and represented a 12 percent discount to net asset value.
Pilot was established to invest in small UK-quoted companies, and aims to create value by providing management of companies in which it invests with support as they grow their businesses.
"This letter is also about your choice between short term optimism and the constructive creation of long term value," it said.
It said Pilot's recent performance had been poor due to it being overweight in recovery stocks, and said it was reviewing the position.
Also, it had taken action to strengthen its investment team.

It had put fund manager Rutherford Asset Management on notice that if Pilot's performance did not exceed the FT Fledgling Index ex Investment Trusts in the year to March 31, 1998, directors would take further action.
It said it was aware some shareholders wanted to realise their capital in Pilot, and it would hold meetings no later than May on the issue.
It would ask shareholders to pass a resolution to keep it as an investment trust. If this was defeated it would put forward two other resolutions.

One would seek to reconstitute Pilot into a successor trust with the same policy after disposing of the proportion of Pilot's underlying investments attributable to shareholders who wish to realise their investments. The other would reconstitute Pilot as an open-ended investment company with the same investment policy.
If all these were defeated, it would propose to liquidate Pilot.
